size.note: Adults 3.5-6 cm snout to vent, to ~11 cm in all (the tail about as long as the body), 1-3 g; lungless, slender, short-legged. Drawn at 0.05 m snout to vent and a 0.05 m tail (0.10 m straight), the trunk 8 mm across, the back 7 mm up at mid-body, the belly a fraction of a millimetre off the ground (it walks low, the belly nearly dragging), toe span 2.7 cm with the legs splayed. length_m here is total length (snout to tail tip); shoulder_or_wingspan_m is the back's height.

source.original: text-to-3D preview, ai_model meshy-6-lite, triangle remesh to 20,000 faces: 20,946 triangles, one piece, untextured; a slender salamander walking with the legs splayed, standing 0.1 units off the midline, its tail curled round to one side
source.prompt: A western red-backed salamander (Plethodon vehiculum), a small slender woodland salamander, NOT a lizard, NOT a newt, no scales, smooth moist skin. One adult walking on the ground, side-on pose, body straight, four short thin legs splayed out to the sides with small toes. Realistic proportions: 10 cm long, the round tapering tail as long as the body, a slender cylindrical body with fine grooves along the sides, a small rounded head a little wider than the neck, small dark bulging eyes. A broad straight-edged reddish-orange stripe down the back from the head to the tail tip, dark grey-black sides with fine white flecks, a grey belly. No base, no ground. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

attributes: _BLUE (0 everywhere: no blue patches; kept so the shader path is the lizard's)

rig: reptile template (as the western fence lizard's, tools/build_fence_lizard.py; the client draws it with the lizard's spine wave and sprawling walk): BODY 0, LEG_A 1 (left fore, right hind) and LEG_B 2 (right fore, left hind) splayed, pivots at the shoulder and hip rings (found from the geometry: limb vertices outside the trunk's half-width or under the belly, connected to a foot); HEAD 6 (pivot at the neck, 20% of snout-vent behind the snout); TAIL 3 (inner half, pivot at the vent) and TAIL_TIP 8 (outer half, pivot mid-tail, child of TAIL). extras.rig (kind 'reptile'): head, tail, tail_tip, fore, hind, legs (FL FR HL HR), snout_z, vent_z, tail_end_z, belly_y, back_y, drop, blue_off and throat_off (the belly grey; nothing is blue), length_m. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Generated (one meshy-6-lite preview, 5 credits). Reads as a red-backed salamander: a slender, low, cylindrical body with short thin splayed legs and small toes, a small rounded head, a round tapering tail as long as the body laid straight behind on the ground; the field mark, a broad reddish-orange dorsal stripe with straight sharp edges (cut into the mesh as straight lines and kept through the collapse) from the back of the head to the tail tip, narrowing with the tail; dark grey-black sides with sparse pale flecks, a grey belly mottled pale, the upper arm and thigh washed with the stripe colour, dark grey limbs. Still wrong or unchecked: the preview's tail curled to one side and was carried onto a straight axis by arc length (its cross-section kept, so it can look a little faceted); the head is as wide as the body (the generator gave no neck); the costal grooves are not modelled; the flecks are face-sized (only on small faces, so lod0 shows a sparse scatter, lod1 and lod2 none); the eyes are dark faces on a dark head and barely show; the lod2 stripe is a ragged band of whole faces; the belly almost touches the ground (0.3 mm), as a walking plethodontid's does but the client's lizard pose may sink it; only the red-striped form is drawn (the tan, yellow and unstriped dark morphs are not).
